original_value: Ship detection from high-resolution optical satellite images is still an important task that deserves optimal solutions. This paper introduces a novel high-resolution image network-based approach based on the preselection of a region of interest (RoI). This pre-selected network first identifies and extracts a region of interest from input images. In order to efficiently match ship candidates, the principle of our approach is to distinguish suspected areas from the images based on hue, saturation, value (HSV) differences between ships and the background. The whole approach is the basis of an experiment with a large ship dataset, consisting of Google Earth images and HRSC2016 datasets. The experiment shows that the H-YOLO network, which uses the same weight training from a set of remote sensing images, has a 19.01% higher recognition rate and a 16.19% higher accuracy than applying the you only look once (YOLO) network alone. After image preprocessing, the value of the intersection over union (IoU) is also greatly improved.

result.paraphrase: Detecting ships in high-resolution optical satellite imagery remains an important problem that calls for effective solutions. This paper proposes a new high-resolution image network approach built around preselecting a region of interest (RoI). The preselected network first locates and extracts the RoI from the input images. To match ship candidates efficiently, the method separates suspected regions by leveraging hue, saturation, and value (HSV) differences between ships and the background. The full approach is evaluated through experiments on a large ship dataset made up of Google Earth images and HRSC2016 data. The results show that the H-YOLO network, trained with the same weights from a remote sensing image set, achieves a 19.01% higher recognition rate and 16.19% higher accuracy than using the YOLO network alone. Image preprocessing also substantially improves the intersection over union (IoU) value.
